name: Tripeptide-3

lead: Tripeptide-3 is a short synthetic peptide used in cosmetics, including products aimed at reducing facial oiliness. People with oily skin look to it for less shine and a more matte face.

Little is published under this name. A 2024 pharmaceutics study developed nanoemulsions to deliver Tripeptide-3 to the skin and reported that, in healthy volunteers over 28 days, the formulation decreased sebum production and increased skin moisture. The study focused on getting the hydrophilic peptide into skin; the abstract does not describe how it affects sebum.

paras: It is used in leave-on oil-control serums and lotions applied to the face as part of a daily routine. In the 2024 study, changes were measured over 28 days.
The study included an irritation assessment, though details are limited. No wider safety literature was found.

angle.text: Tripeptide-3 appears in products marketed for oil control, so oily skin looks less shiny and more matte. The aim is lower sebum, which reduces facial oiliness. A 2024 delivery study reported lower sebum and higher moisture in volunteers over 28 days.

lead: Tripeptide-3 is an INCI name for a short synthetic peptide used in cosmetics, including products aimed at reducing facial oiliness. Little is published about it under this name.

A 2024 pharmaceutics study developed nanoemulsions to deliver Tripeptide-3 to the skin and reported that, in healthy volunteers over 28 days, the formulation decreased sebum production and increased skin moisture [1].

paras: The cosmetic use examined in the literature is control of excess facial sebum, with the peptide delivered in emulsion-based products [1].

The 2024 study combined formulation development with a test in healthy volunteers. It tested the nanoemulsion for skin irritation and oil-control over 28 days and reported reduced sebum and improved moisture [1]. The abstract does not describe a placebo-controlled design, and the study concerns the delivery system as much as the peptide itself.
